# Quarto 2 {#sec-q2}

Quarto 2 is in development. 
The examples in this book use syntax that works in Quarto 1 and Quarto 2 where possible. 
This appendix lists the cases where that is not possible. 

## More characters need to be escaped 

@sec-escaping explains how to escape characters that markdown uses for syntax.
In many cases, Quarto 1 will correctly guess when you meant to show a literal character.
Quarto 2 never guesses: a character is read as the start of markup and Quarto 2 stops with an error if the markup does not end.

Consequently, you'll find you need to escape more characters in Quarto 2.
For example, each line below works in Quarto 1:

```markdown
Edit _quarto.yml and _brand.yml.
It costs $5 and $10.
Pass { a, b } to the function.
A lone ` in prose.
The `a.rs`'s module.
```

 In Quarto 2, each line is an error:

| Line           | Quarto 2 error                              |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `_quarto.yml`  | Q-2-5, unclosed underscore emphasis         |
| `$5`           | parse error, `$` starts inline math         |
| `{ a, b }`     | parse error, braces are only for attributes |
| a lone `` ` `` | parse error, `` ` `` starts a code span     |
| `` `a.rs`'s `` | Q-2-7, `'` after a code span starts a quote |

To fix the errors, escape each character with a backslash: 

```markdown
Edit \_quarto.yml and \_brand.yml.
It costs \$5 and \$10.
Pass \{ a, b \} to the function.
A lone \` in prose.
The `a.rs`\'s module.
```

The backslashes are harmless in Quarto 1, so this example will render in both Quarto 1 and Quarto 2.

If the text is code, use a code span instead, for example `` `_quarto.yml` ``.

## Footnotes with more than one paragraph

@sec-footnotes describes the footnote syntax.
In Quarto 1 a multi-paragraph footnote uses indentation:

```markdown
Here is some text that needs a long footnote.[^longnote]

[^longnote]: Here's the footnote contents with multiple blocks.

    Subsequent paragraphs are indented to show that they
    belong to the previous footnote.
```

In Quarto 2, a multi-paragraph footnote needs to be in a fenced div:

```markdown
Here is some text that needs a long footnote.[^longnote]

::: ^longnote
Here's the footnote contents with multiple blocks.

Subsequent paragraphs are not indented. The div holds them.
:::
```

These syntaxes are exclusive, Quarto 2 does not accept the indented paragraph and Quarto 1 does not
recognize the fenced div as a footnote.

A footnote with one paragraph uses the same syntax in both versions.

## Math macros

@sec-equations-macros describes how to define macros.
In Quarto 1, you can define `\newcommand` in the body of the document, outside any `$` or `$$`. 
The macros then apply to all the math in the document:

```markdown
\newcommand{\R}{\mathbb{R}}
\newcommand{\vect}[1]{\mathbf{#1}}
\newcommand{\Var}{\operatorname{Var}}

For any $\vect{x} \in \R^n$,

$$
\Var(\vect{x}) \geq 0.
$$
```

Quarto 2 does not accept a `\newcommand` outside math and inside math `\newcommand` only applies to the math expression that contains it. 

In Quarto 2, you must put each definition in each expression that uses the macro:

```markdown
For any $\newcommand{\R}{\mathbb{R}}\newcommand{\vect}[1]{\mathbf{#1}}\vect{x} \in \R^n$,

$$
\newcommand{\vect}[1]{\mathbf{#1}}
\newcommand{\Var}{\operatorname{Var}}
\Var(\vect{x}) \geq 0.
$$
```

You can use this syntax in Quarto 1, but it repeats each definition.
@sec-equations-macros also shows how to share macros between documents with an include
file, for example `_macros.qmd`. 
In Quarto 2, this does not work.
